title: Azure / Managed Redis / Overview
description: Azure Managed Redis (Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise): inventory and per-cluster Azure Monitor metrics. Managed by Terraform (azure-managed-grafana): edit dashboards/redis/azure-managed-redis-overview.json, not the dashboard in the UI. Changes made in Grafana are overwritten on the next apply. Builds on Microsoft's official 'Azure Managed Redis' dashboard (grafana.com/grafana/dashboards/24988, published by the azure org): same Summary/Performance/Operations/Connectivity sections, plus inventory, per-node/per-shard splits and replication panels, with rate metrics on Average aggregation as Microsoft Learn now requires.

links.tooltip: Open the selected resource in the Azure portal

panels.title: Troubleshooting - $resource
panels.description: Start here when something looks wrong: is the resource running, has an alert fired, what changed? Resource Graph data; it lags a few minutes behind Azure. Grafana's identity needs read access (Monitoring Reader) on the resource.

panels.title: State
panels.description: Current state from Azure Resource Manager. Green: running/ready. Red: stopped, deallocated, failed or disabled. Orange: anything else, e.g. updating or starting.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise' and resourceGroup =~ '$rg' and name =~ '$resource'
| project ['State'] = tostring(properties.resourceState), ['Provisioning'] = tostring(properties.provisioningState)

panels.title: Open alerts
panels.description: Azure Monitor alerts fired on this resource and not closed (alerts are kept 30 days). History across resources: the bundled Azure / Alert Consumption dashboard.

azureResourceGraph.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tolower(tostring(e.targetResource)) == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource')
| where tostring(e.monitorCondition) == 'Fired' and tostring(e.alertState) != 'Closed'
| summarize ['Open alerts'] = count()

panels.title: Changes (time range)
panels.description: Resource Manager changes to this resource and its child resources in the time range (Resource Graph change history, kept 14 days). Details on the right.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| summarize Changes = count()

panels.title: What changed
panels.description: Latest Resource Manager changes in the time range: who changed what, with which operation, and which properties. A change just before a problem started is the first suspect.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| project Time = todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp),
          Change = tostring(properties.changeType),
          Resource = iff(target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource'), '(this resource)', substring(target, strlen(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/$resource')) + 1)),
          ['Changed by'] = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.changedBy),
          Operation = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.operation),
          Properties = strcat_array(bag_keys(properties.changes), ', ')
| order by Time desc
| take 50

panels.title: Inventory: all Azure Managed Redis clusters in the subscription
Azure Managed Redis clusters ($sub)
panels.description: All Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise clusters in the selected subscription (Azure Resource Graph). The same resource type also hosts the Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise / Enterprise Flash tiers (SKU Enterprise_* / EnterpriseFlash_*), which retire on 2027-03-31; the 'offering' column flags them.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.cache/redisenterprise'
| extend skuName = tostring(sku.name), skuCapacity = toint(sku.capacity)
| extend offering = iff(skuName startswith 'Enterprise', 'Cache for Redis Enterprise (retires 2027-03-31)', 'Azure Managed Redis')
| project name, resourceGroup, location, sku = skuName, capacity = skuCapacity, offering, redisVersion = tostring(properties.redisVersion), highAvailability = tostring(properties.highAvailability), provisioningState = tostring(properties.provisioningState), resourceState = tostring(properties.resourceState), zones = tostring(zones)
| order by name asc

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Max CPU across nodes (percentProcessorTime, Maximum). Microsoft recommends this over Server load.

panels.title: Server load
panels.description: serverLoad, Maximum (cluster level). Can report values above 100 on Azure Managed Redis; check CPU too.

panels.title: Used memory
panels.description: usedmemorypercentage, Maximum.

panels.title: Connected clients
panels.description: connectedclients, Maximum (busiest node).

panels.title: Operations / s
panels.description: operationsPerSecond, Maximum (all shards).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: hits / (hits + misses) over the selected time range, from the cachehits and cachemisses rates (Average). A low ratio is normal for some cache-aside workloads.

panels.title: Cache read
panels.description: cacheRead, Maximum (network ingress).

panels.title: Cache write
panels.description: cacheWrite, Maximum (network egress).

panels.title: CPU, server load & memory
panels.description: percentProcessorTime, serverLoad and usedmemorypercentage, all Maximum.

panels.title: CPU by node
panels.description: percentProcessorTime, Maximum, split by InstanceId.

panels.title: Cache read / write bandwidth
panels.description: cacheRead and cacheWrite, Maximum.

panels.title: Cache latency by node
panels.description: cacheLatency (microseconds, proxy-forwarded requests), Average, split by InstanceId. Only reported while there is traffic.

panels.title: Operations per second
panels.description: operationsPerSecond (Maximum) and totalcommandsprocessed (rate, Average).

panels.title: Gets / sets per second
panels.description: getcommands and setcommands (rates, Average).

panels.title: Cache hits / misses per second
panels.description: cachehits and cachemisses (rates, Average).

panels.title: Used memory
panels.description: usedmemory, Maximum. With high availability it includes primary and replica, so it can look 2x.

panels.title: Shard memory used by slot range
panels.description: ShardMemoryUsedBytes (preview), Maximum, split by Slots. A max/min ratio > 2x means imbalance.

panels.title: Shard memory used: primary vs replica
panels.description: ShardMemoryUsedBytes (preview), Maximum across shards, split by Role (primary / replica).

panels.title: Total keys
panels.description: totalkeys, Maximum. On clustered caches this is the key count of the largest shard.

panels.title: Shard key count by slot range
panels.description: ShardKeyCount (preview), Maximum, split by Slots.

panels.title: Evicted / expired keys per second
panels.description: evictedkeys and expiredkeys (rates, Average). Evictions mean memory pressure.

panels.title: Connected clients by node
panels.description: connectedclients, Maximum, split by InstanceId.

panels.title: Geo-replication healthy
panels.description: geoReplicationHealthy, Minimum (1 healthy, 0 unhealthy). Only for caches in an active geo-replication group; patching can cause short dips.

panels.title: Shard replication link up by slot range
panels.description: ShardReplicationLinkUp (preview), Minimum, split by Slots. Emitted by replica shards only; 0 for a long period (e.g. 120 min) means the replica lost its primary.

panels.title: Replica output buffer memory by slot range
panels.description: ShardMemoryClientsReplicaBytes (preview), Maximum, split by Slots. Steady growth means the replica cannot keep up.

panels.title: Shard memory: normal client buffers by slot range
panels.description: ShardMemoryClientsNormalBytes (preview), Maximum, split by Slots: input/output buffers of non-replica clients.
